summary: New Emitter class; the removal test is a negative test without a positive control, and once() is checked with a single emit.

defects.description: `does not call a listener after it is removed` subscribes to "save" but emits "close", so it passes even if off()/the unsubscribe function does nothing (`set?.delete(fn)` removed, or the returned closure emptied, survives). It is a negative test without a positive control; it must emit "save" after unsubscribing.

`once listeners fire once` emits a single time and checks `toHaveBeenCalled()`, so removing the `off()` call inside once (listener fires on every emit) survives. It should emit twice and assert toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1) with the first payload.
listenerCount and the cleanup of empty listener sets in off() have no coverage at all (NoCoverage mutants). Lower priority than the two above.
